drinks.name: Brewed Coffee (drip/filter)
drinks.notes: USDA SR Legacy 'Beverages, coffee, brewed, prepared with tap water' (FNDDS 2710375 identical). Per-100 g = per-100 mL (density ~1.00). Caffeine varies widely: McCusker et al. 2003 (J Anal Toxicol 27:520) measured 58-259 mg per 16-oz specialty coffee (~12-55 mg/100 mL), and the same Starbucks Breakfast Blend ranged 259-564 mg/16 oz over six days; Starbucks currently publishes ~310-315 mg per grande Pike Place (~66 mg/100 mL). USDA's 40 mg/100 mL (~95 mg per 8 oz) is a typical home-brew value. Range upper bound set to 70 to cover large chain brews; extreme outliers exist. UK CoFID 'coffee, infusion, average' cross-check: ~2 kcal/100 g, consistent.

drinks.name: Decaf Brewed Coffee
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'coffee, brewed, prepared with tap water, decaffeinated'. Decaf is NOT caffeine-free: McCusker et al. 2006 (J Anal Toxicol 30:611) found 0-13.9 mg per 16-oz cup in 10 outlets (0-2.9 mg/100 mL); Starbucks brewed decaf 12.0-13.4 mg per 16 oz.

drinks.name: Iced Coffee (brewed, over ice)
drinks.notes: FNDDS 'Iced Coffee, brewed' - values are lower than hot brewed coffee because the recipe includes melted ice. Unsweetened, black.

drinks.name: Cold Brew Coffee (ready to drink)

source.name: Derived: USDA brewed coffee nutrients (FDC 171890); caffeine from Starbucks published value; range from Fuller & Rao 2017

drinks.notes: No USDA record for cold brew. Nutrients use brewed coffee as proxy (black cold brew ~5 kcal per 16 oz per Starbucks). Default caffeine = Starbucks grande cold brew 205 mg/473 mL (43.3 mg/100 mL); Nitro grande ~280 mg. Lane et al. 2017 reported ~207 mg per 12 oz (58 mg/100 mL) for a commercial cold brew. Fuller & Rao 2017 (Sci Rep 7:17979) brewed at 1:10 coffee:water and measured 990-1230 mg/L (99-123 mg/100 mL), vs 840-1060 mg/L for hot brew at the same ratio: cold brew is not inherently stronger; its caffeine depends on the grind:water ratio and dilution. Undiluted concentrates should be diluted ~1:1 or logged with a custom caffeine value.

drinks.name: Decaf Espresso
drinks.notes: USDA SR lists only 1 mg caffeine/100 g, but McCusker et al. 2006 measured 3.0-15.8 mg per 1-oz decaf shot at Starbucks (~10-53 mg/100 mL). The default keeps USDA's value; the range warns that real decaf shots can be meaningful for caffeine-sensitive users.

drinks.name: Espresso (double shot / doppio)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'coffee, brewed, espresso, restaurant-prepared' (FNDDS 2710378 identical): 212 mg caffeine/100 g (~64 mg per 30 mL shot). Shots vary by dose, volume and chain: McCusker 2003 measured 75.8 mg in one shot and 140.4 mg in two short shots at a US shop; Starbucks publishes ~75 mg per shot; per-volume concentration therefore ranges roughly 150-300 mg/100 mL (ristretto is more concentrated, lungo less). Serving conventions: Italy/EU single ~25 mL, US single ~30 mL (1 fl oz), double/doppio ~60 mL. Same per-100 mL data as single; only the default serving differs.

drinks.name: Espresso (single shot)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'coffee, brewed, espresso, restaurant-prepared' (FNDDS 2710378 identical): 212 mg caffeine/100 g (~64 mg per 30 mL shot). Serving conventions: Italy/EU single ~25 mL, US single ~30 mL (1 fl oz), double/doppio ~60 mL.

drinks.name: Cappuccino
drinks.notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, Cappuccino' (unsweetened; recipe has more foam/air and less milk per gram than latte). Density 1.02 g/mL (foam lowers it; approximate). Traditional Italian cappuccino ~150-180 mL; US chains 240-590 mL. Starbucks grande cappuccino = 150 mg caffeine.

drinks.name: Flat White

source.name: Matvaretabellen (Norwegian Food Composition Table) food 13.040 'Caffe latte, single, with whole milk' for all nutrients (per 100 g: water 89.0, 59 kcal, protein 3.1, fat 3.2, carbs 4.6, sugars 4, Na 35, K 152) x 1.03 g/mL; Starbucks published caffeine (grande flat white 195 mg)
source.crossCheck: Starbucks grande (473 mL) Flat White, whole milk, per US nutrition listings: 220 kcal, 11 g fat, 18 g carbs, 17 g sugar, 12 g protein, 150 mg sodium (= 46.5 kcal, 2.3 g fat, 3.8 g carbs, 3.6 g sugar, 2.5 g protein, 31.7 mg Na per 100 mL).

drinks.notes: No USDA record. A flat white is espresso (often ristretto) with steamed whole milk and thin microfoam. All nutrients are from one record, Norway's whole-milk caffe latte (Matvaretabellen 13.040; verified Nov 2026: 59 kcal, 3.1 g protein, 3.2 g fat, 4.6 g carbs, 4 g sugars, 35 mg Na, 152 mg K per 100 g), converted with density 1.03; the sodium and potassium happen to equal the FNDDS latte values but are sourced from the Norwegian record. This is a latte proxy: Starbucks' grande flat white (more espresso per mL, whole milk) works out to ~46.5 kcal, 3.6 g sugar, 2.5 g protein and 32 mg Na per 100 mL, about 20-25% lower than this record, so the per-100 mL values are an upper-side estimate for chain flat whites. Caffeine default = Starbucks grande flat white 195 mg/473 mL (41 mg/100 mL); a classic 160-180 mL Australian/UK flat white with a double shot (~130-150 mg) is ~75-85 mg/100 mL, hence the wide range.

drinks.name: Black Tea (brewed)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'tea, black, brewed, prepared with tap water' (~47 mg caffeine per 8 oz). Chin et al. 2008 (J Anal Toxicol 32:702) measured 14-61 mg caffeine per 6- or 8-oz serving across 20 white, green and black teas (~6-36 mg/100 mL), with no consistent trend by tea type; steep time mattered more. UK CoFID weak black tea infusion lists ~18 mg potassium/100 g, so potassium varies with strength. Milk is a modifier (UK default often includes milk).

drinks.name: Decaf Black Tea
drinks.notes: USDA SR decaffeinated brewed black tea. Chin et al. 2008: decaf teas contained <12 mg per serving (<5 mg/100 mL).

drinks.name: Green Tea (brewed)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'tea, green, brewed, regular' (~28 mg per 8 oz). Chin et al. 2008 (J Anal Toxicol 32:702) measured 14-61 mg caffeine per 6- or 8-oz serving across 20 white, green and black teas (~6-36 mg/100 mL), with no consistent trend by tea type; steep time mattered more. Japanese Standard Tables list sencha infusion at 20 mg/100 mL and gyokuro at 160 mg/100 mL (via secondary summary), showing how much leaf type and dose matter.

drinks.name: Barley tea (mugicha / boricha)

source.name: Japan Standard Tables of Food Composition (8th rev., 2023 suppl.), MEXT: food 16055, barley tea, infusion

drinks.notes: MEXT per 100 g: 99.7 g water, 1 kcal, protein trace, 0.3 g carbohydrate, 1 mg sodium, 6 mg potassium (density taken as 1.00). It is brewed from roasted barley grain, not the tea plant, so it is naturally caffeine-free (caffeine set to 0 on that basis; the MEXT data page does not list caffeine). Protein is 'Tr' (trace) and sugar is not reported, so both are null. Drunk iced in Japan and Korea (boricha); bottled unsweetened versions are equivalent.

drinks.name: Herbal Tea (generic, e.g., peppermint)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'tea, herb, other than chamomile, brewed'. Caffeine-free (Chin et al. 2008 detected no caffeine in herbal teas). Note: yerba mate and guayusa are NOT caffeine-free and should not use this entry.

drinks.name: Hibiscus Tea
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'tea, hibiscus, brewed'. Caffeine-free. Agua de jamaica is usually sweetened - add a sugar modifier.

drinks.name: Matcha (whisked with water)

source.name: Japan Standard Tables of Food Composition 2020 (8th ed., 2023 supplement), food 16035 'matcha' (powder) per 100 g: water 5.0 g, 237 kcal, protein 29.6 g, fat 5.3 g, carbohydrate 39.5 g (fibre 38.5 g), Na 6 mg, K 2700 mg; caffeine 3.2 g/100 g as previously cited; derived per 100 mL

drinks.notes: Derived: 2 g matcha powder whisked into 240 mL water (~242 g of drink). Macros scale the MEXT powder values by 2/242: ~2 kcal, 0.24 g protein, 0.04 g fat, 0.33 g carbohydrate (almost all fibre; available carbohydrate is only 1.6 g/100 g powder, so sugar ~0), 0.05 mg Na and 22 mg K per 100 mL, plus whatever minerals the user's water carries. Caffeine: 32 mg/g (~64 mg per 2 g) = 26.7 mg/100 mL; the caffeine figure comes from the MEXT table notes via secondary summaries and was not displayed on the database page. Published per-gram values span ~19-44 mg/g and doses span 1-4 g, and traditional usucha uses ~2 g in only ~70 mL (~90 mg/100 mL), hence the wide range. Matcha lattes: build as matcha + milk modifier.

drinks.name: Yerba mate (brewed / gourd)

source.crossCheck: FNDDS 2710502 per 100 g: 99.7 g water, 1 kcal, 0.2 g carbs, 1 mg Na, 9 mg K.

drinks.notes: Caffeine measured by Bastos et al. on Brazilian brands: one gourd ('cuia', ~500 mL of successive infusions) of chimarrão = 135 mg (27 mg/100 mL); one cuia of cold tereré = 85 mg (17 mg/100 mL); one 182 mL cup of tea-bag mate cocido = 13 mg (7 mg/100 mL). Default is chimarrão; the range covers all three. Real intake depends heavily on leaf load and the number of refills. Macros come from FNDDS herbal tea, whose description explicitly includes mate tea; unlike other herbal teas, mate is caffeinated (Part B's tea_herbal note says not to use it for mate).

drinks.name: Bubble Tea / Boba Milk Tea

source.name: USDA FoodData Central FNDDS 2021-2023 'Tea, bubble' (FDC 2710508) for water, energy, carbs, protein, fat, Na, K; sugar = representative shop value from three lab analyses (Min et al. 2017; CHOICE AU; Hong Kong CFS 2019); caffeine = Hong Kong CFS/Consumer Council 2013 measured Taiwanese-style milk tea

drinks.notes: FNDDS 'Tea, bubble' re-pulled directly from USDA (per 100 g: water 86.24, 55 kcal, carbs 10.35, sugars 3.5, protein 0.39, fat 1.39, Na 9, K 17, caffeine 8 mg); converted with density 1.04. The FNDDS sugar (3.5 g/100 g) is far below measured shop drinks, so sugarG is a representative shop value instead: Min et al. 2017 (bomb calorimetry + HPLC, Los Angeles shop, 16 oz) measured 37.7 g sugars in 473 mL of milk tea liquid = 8.0 g/100 mL (plus 6.5 g in 60 g pearls); CHOICE (21 Australian bubble teas) averaged 6.3 g/100 g; Hong Kong CFS (2018 samples, regular sugar level) averaged 5.0 g/100 g (range 1.6-7.3) for pearl milk tea. Representative 6.5 g/100 mL; plausible range ~1.7-8 g/100 mL (less-sugar orders lower, brown-sugar drinks higher). Hong Kong CFS measured energy 78 kcal/100 g (58-94) including pearls, above the FNDDS 55 kcal/100 g, so energy is probably conservative. Caffeine: USDA FNDDS lists 8 mg/100 g (recipe-based); Hong Kong CFS/Consumer Council 2013 measured 10 Taiwanese-style milk teas at 250-490 mg/L (mean 320 mg/L), so 32 mg/100 mL default with range 8-49. Fruit teas without a tea base, and taro/milk slushes, can be far lower. The pearls are eaten, not drunk; the hydration agent may want to discount them.

Water, sugar (0), sodium and potassium remain from the USDA record as generic strong-beer values. Strong beers span ~8-12% ABV; imperial stouts and barley wines usually carry more residual carbohydrate (and kcal) than DIPAs, so offer a custom ABV.

drinks.name: Hard Cider (~5% ABV)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'AMBER, hard cider' (4.0 g alcohol/100 g -> ~5.1% ABV). Sweetness varies widely by brand (dry ciders ~1-3 g sugar/100 mL, sweet US ciders up to ~6-7). UK ciders range 4-7.5% ABV.

drinks.name: Aperol Spritz

source.name: Composite: 90 mL Prosecco (USDA FNDDS 'Wine, sparkling' 2710687) + 60 mL Aperol (EU label: 159 kcal, 26.1 g sugar per 100 mL, 11% vol) + 30 mL club soda (USDA SR 174842)
source.crossCheck: The same Aperol per-100 mL panel is reproduced by the Frankfurt Airport shop listing (159.2 kcal, 26.13 g sugar, 0.05 g salt).

drinks.notes: Recipe (official 3-2-1): 90 mL Prosecco + 60 mL Aperol + 30 mL soda = 180 mL, ice ignored. Per drink: 163 kcal, 16.6 g sugar (mostly from Aperol), 13.7 g ethanol = 1.0 US standard drinks; ~9.7% ABV in the glass. Water, sodium and potassium are null because Aperol's label gives no water or potassium (its 0.05 g salt/100 mL implies ~20 mg Na but was not used). Prosecco density assumed 0.995.

drinks.name: Bloody Mary
drinks.notes: FNDDS recipe: 2 fl oz 80-proof spirit + 5.5 fl oz seasoned tomato juice + Worcestershire, horseradish and chili. Per 100 g: 73 kcal, 2.3 g sugar, 200 mg sodium, 166 mg potassium, 7.8 g ethanol. Density 1.02 assumed (tomato-juice base ~1.03, offset by ethanol) = 10.1% ABV. One drink (225 g) = 17.6 g ethanol = 1.3 US standard drinks and ~450 mg sodium. A Canadian Caesar made with Clamato is saltier still.

drinks.name: Cosmopolitan

source.name: Composite from USDA: 40 mL 80-proof vodka (SR 174818) + 15 mL orange liqueur (FNDDS 'Liqueur' 2710623, which lists triple sec) + 15 mL lime juice (SR 168156) + 30 mL cranberry juice cocktail (SR 171903)
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Martini, flavored' (2710640) names cosmopolitan among its descriptions, but its recipe is 3.5 fl oz spirit with only a teaspoon of cranberry, so it was not used.

drinks.notes: Recipe (IBA-style): 40 mL vodka + 15 mL triple sec/Cointreau + 15 mL lime juice + 30 mL cranberry juice cocktail = 100 mL before ice dilution (ignored, as in Part B's composites). Densities: vodka 0.948, liqueur 1.014 (FNDDS 30 g/fl oz), lime 1.041 and cranberry 1.069 (USDA portion weights). Per 100 mL drink: 151 kcal, 9.1 g sugar, 15.9 g ethanol = 1.1 US standard drinks. The generic FNDDS liqueur is ~27% ABV; real Cointreau is 40%, which would add ~1.5 g ethanol per drink.

drinks.name: Gin & Tonic

source.name: Composite from USDA SR: 1.5 fl oz 80-proof gin (FDC 174815) + 4 fl oz tonic water (FDC 171869)

drinks.notes: Recipe: 44 mL gin (40%) + 118 mL tonic, ice melt ignored (~163 mL). Per drink ~139 kcal, 10.7 g sugar, 14.0 g ethanol (1 US standard drink). Bar pours vary (UK single 25 mL + 150-200 mL tonic is ~1 unit, ~3% ABV); slimline tonic removes the sugar. Canned G&Ts run 5-7% ABV (CSPI alcohol chart lists Cutwater G&T 6.2% ABV, 230 kcal).

drinks.name: Long Island Iced Tea
drinks.notes: FNDDS recipe: 2.5 fl oz mixed 80-proof spirits + 1 fl oz sour mix + 124 g cola. Per 100 g: 107 kcal, 8.4 g sugar, 5 mg caffeine (from the cola), 10.4 g ethanol (density 1.00 assumed) = 13.2% ABV. One drink (225 g) = 23 g ethanol = 1.7 US standard drinks; bar versions with five half-ounce spirits are similar or stronger. Listed as a Part B v2 gap.

drinks.name: Margarita

source.name: USDA FoodData Central, FDC 2710638 'Margarita', read directly from the FDC portal endpoint (Nov 2026)

corrections.reason: Direct USDA re-pull: water 75.08 and carbs = sugars 16.06 g/100 g; x1.03 gives 77.33 and 16.54 (mirror-derived 77.35 and 16.58). Energy, alcohol, Na, K and ABV confirmed.

drinks.notes: FNDDS 'Margarita' (1 drink = 225 g; 8.2 g alcohol/100 g -> ~8.4 g/100 mL, ~10.7% ABV; density 1.03 assumed). One FNDDS drink holds ~18.5 g ethanol = 1.3 US standard drinks. High sodium reflects the salted rim. Restaurant/frozen margaritas are often larger (12-20 oz) and can contain 2-3 standard drinks; a classic 3-oz-pour on the rocks is smaller but stronger.

drinks.name: Mimosa
drinks.notes: FNDDS recipe: 3 fl oz orange juice + 88 g wine (FNDDS uses white table wine for the sparkling-wine component). Per 100 g: 64 kcal, 4.7 g sugar, 128 mg potassium, 5.0 g ethanol (density 1.00 assumed) = 6.3% ABV. One FNDDS drink (180 g) = 9 g ethanol = 0.6 US standard drinks. A 50/50 flute with Prosecco is similar; more wine raises the alcohol.

drinks.name: Mojito
drinks.notes: FNDDS recipe: 2 fl oz 80-proof rum + 5.5 fl oz club soda + 16 g lime + 1 tsp sugar + an herb sprig (FNDDS uses cilantro as the herb stand-in for mint). Per 100 g: 61 kcal, 1.8 g sugar, 7.6 g ethanol (density assumed 1.00) = 9.6% ABV. One drink (225 g) = 17 g ethanol = 1.2 US standard drinks. Bar mojitos made with simple syrup are often sweeter.

drinks.name: Moscow Mule
drinks.notes: FNDDS recipe: 56 g 80-proof vodka (2 fl oz) + 165 g ginger ale + 5 g sugar (USDA has no ginger beer record, so ginger ale plus sugar stands in for the sweeter ginger beer); lime is not included. Per 100 g: 91 kcal, 8.7 g sugar, 8.3 g ethanol (density 1.00 assumed) = 10.5% ABV. One drink (225 g) = 18.7 g ethanol = 1.3 US standard drinks.

drinks.name: Piña Colada
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'pina colada, prepared-from-recipe' (9.9 g alcohol/100 g; density 1.05 assumed -> ~10.4 g/100 mL, ~13% ABV). Very energy-dense (~435 kcal per 8 oz).

drinks.name: Rum & Cola (Cuba Libre)

source.name: Composite from USDA SR: 1.5 fl oz 80-proof rum (FDC 174815) + 4 fl oz cola (FDC 174852)

drinks.notes: Recipe: 44 mL rum (40%) + 118 mL regular cola (~163 mL). Per drink ~149 kcal, ~12.2 g sugar, 14.0 g ethanol (1 US standard drink), ~11 mg caffeine from the cola. Diet cola removes nearly all sugar; same template works for whiskey & cola or vodka & soda (use club soda: 0 kcal).

drinks.name: Sangria (red)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Sangria, white' (2710696): 83 kcal, 6.3 g sugar, 7.9 g alcohol per 100 g.

drinks.notes: FNDDS recipe: 750 g red table wine + 6 fl oz liqueur + 16 fl oz club soda + lemon juice + 1/8 cup sugar. Per 100 g: 85 kcal, 6.1 g sugar, 8.0 g ethanol (density assumed 1.00, since sugar and ethanol roughly offset) = 10.1% ABV. One FNDDS glass (228 g) = 18 g ethanol = 1.3 US standard drinks. Fruit pieces are not drunk and are not included. Pitcher recipes vary (more juice means less alcohol and more sugar).

drinks.name: Whiskey Sour
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'whiskey sour' (14.1 g alcohol/100 g; density 1.02 assumed -> ~14.4 g/100 mL, ~18% ABV). Sugars field uses carbohydrate (sugar not separately reported; it is essentially all sugar from sour mix).

drinks.name: Flavored Malt Beverage / Hard Lemonade
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'malt beer, hard lemonade' (~5.2% ABV). NIAAA notes flavored malt beverages are often ~7% ABV (8-10 oz = 1 standard drink); 'Twisted Tea'/'Mike's Harder' variants reach 8%.

drinks.name: Hard kombucha (~6% ABV)

source.name: JuneShine Ocean Squeeze product page (manufacturer nutrition panel)
source.crossCheck: Other JuneShine flavors (manufacturer pages, via search): 105-155 kcal, 2-5 g sugar, 6-8 g carbs per 12 oz, all 6% ABV.

drinks.notes: Manufacturer panel per 12 fl oz (355 mL): 155 kcal, 8 g carbs, 5 g sugar, 45 mg sodium, 6% ABV (4.7 g ethanol/100 mL; 16.8 g per can = 1.2 US standard drinks). Made on a fermented green-tea base, so some caffeine is likely, but none is declared (null). Water and protein are not on the panel (null). Non-alcoholic kombucha (<0.5%) is other_kombucha.

drinks.name: Hard Seltzer (5% ABV)

source.name: White Claw label (12 oz, via US retailer listings); FNDDS Hard seltzer (FDC 2710622) cross-check

drinks.notes: White Claw per 12 oz: 100 kcal, 2 g carbs/sugar, 20 mg sodium, 5% ABV -> 3.95 g ethanol/100 mL, 14.0 g per can = 1 US standard drink. FNDDS 'Hard seltzer' (24 kcal, 0.55 g carbs, 17 mg Na, 6 mg K, 3.2 g alcohol per 100 g ~= 4% ABV) is a lighter generic; potassium taken from it. Many brands also sell 8% versions (e.g., White Claw Surge) - use a custom ABV.

drinks.name: Coffee liqueur (Kahlúa-type)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Liqueur, coffee flavored' (2710625; Kahlua, Tia Maria) reproduces the SR values.

drinks.notes: USDA SR per 100 g: 38.3 g sugar, 46.8 g carbs, 26 mg caffeine, 21.7 g alcohol, 336 kcal; density 1.177 g/mL from USDA's 34.8 g per fl oz. ALCOHOL INCONSISTENCY: 21.7 g/100 g x 1.177 would mean ~32% ABV, but the record is labelled 53 proof (26.5%). alcoholG therefore uses the stated proof (26.5% x 0.789 = 20.9 g/100 mL), and energy = USDA non-alcohol energy (336 - 21.7 x 6.93) x density + 20.9 g x 6.93. Current US Kahlúa and Tia Maria are 20% ABV (~16 g/100 mL), so this overstates alcohol for them. Caffeine ~13 mg per 1.5 fl oz pour.

drinks.name: Cream liqueur (Baileys-type)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.description: Alcoholic beverage, liqueur, coffee with cream, 34 proof
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Liqueur, cream' (2710624; lists Bailey's Irish Cream, RumChata) is a recipe estimate with 33.5 g sugar and 2.7 g fat per 100 g and ~25% ABV, less like Baileys than the SR record.

drinks.notes: USDA SR per 100 g: 327 kcal, 19.8 g sugar, 15.7 g fat, 2.8 g protein, 92 mg sodium, 8 mg caffeine, 13.8 g alcohol; density 1.052 from USDA's 31.1 g per fl oz. The computed 14.5 g ethanol/100 mL = 18.4% ABV is slightly above the record's stated 34 proof (17%) and Baileys' 17%, so standard-drink counts are ~8% conservative. A 1.5 fl oz (44 mL) pour = 6.4 g ethanol (0.5 US standard drink) and ~150 kcal.

drinks.name: Soju (Korean, green bottle)

source.name: Label ABV: Jinro Chamisul Fresh 360 mL, 16% (LCBO product listing)
source.crossCheck: ABV varies by market and year: 15.7-17.8% for 'fresh' green-bottle soju; flavored fruit soju ~12-13%. A UK retailer panel lists 95 kcal/100 mL for a 16.9% Chamisul Fresh.

drinks.notes: Only the alcohol is sourced: 16% ABV x 0.789 = 12.6 g ethanol/100 mL, so a 360 mL bottle holds ~45 g ethanol (3.2 US standard drinks) and a 50 mL soju glass ~6.3 g. Ethanol alone supplies ~88 kcal/100 mL; total energy, sugar and water were not found from a primary source, so they are null. Flavored soju (~13%, sweetened) has more sugar and less alcohol.

drinks.name: Spirits, 40% ABV (vodka, gin, rum, whiskey, tequila)
searchTerms: spirits, 40% abv (vodka, gin, rum, whiskey, tequila)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'distilled, all (gin, rum, vodka, whiskey) 80 proof': 33.4 g alcohol/100 g x density 0.948 (40% ethanol-water) = 31.7 g/100 mL = 40% ABV. US shot 1.5 fl oz (44 mL) = 13.9 g = 1 US standard drink; UK single 25 mL = 1 unit (7.9 g), larger UK measure 35 mL; a US 'double' 3 fl oz. All energy is from ethanol (~7 kcal/g). Higher-proof spirits: scale alcohol by ABV (86 proof SR 171919, 100 proof SR 173664).

drinks.name: Mulled wine (glühwein / glögg)
drinks.notes: FNDDS recipe: 147 g red table wine + 1 tsp honey + nutmeg; per 100 g 96 kcal, 4.2 g sugar, 10.1 g ethanol (density 1.00 assumed) = 12.8% ABV. Commercial Christmas-market glühwein is often sweeter and weaker (around 7-10% ABV); Nordic glögg with added spirits can be stronger. One 150 mL mug of the FNDDS recipe = 15 g ethanol = 1.1 US standard drinks.

drinks.name: Non-alcoholic Wine
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'Wine, non-alcoholic'. Many dealcoholised wines contain up to 0.5% ABV and added grape juice (more sugar than this record).

drinks.name: Port / sweet fortified wine

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Wine, dessert, sweet' (2710692; lists sherry, port) reproduces the SR values.

drinks.notes: USDA SR per 100 g: 160 kcal, 7.8 g sugar, 13.7 g carbs, 15.3 g alcohol; density 0.9975 from USDA's 29.5 g per fl oz gives 15.3 g ethanol/100 mL = 19.3% ABV (port is typically 19-20%). A 3 fl oz (90 mL) pour = 13.7 g ethanol = 1 US standard drink. Dry fortified wines (fino sherry, dry vermouth): USDA 'wine, dessert, dry' (175112) has less sugar.

drinks.name: Red Wine
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'wine, table, red': 10.6 g alcohol/100 g x density 0.993 = 10.5 g/100 mL = 13.3% ABV. A US 5 oz (148 mL) pour = 15.6 g ethanol = 1.1 US standard drinks (NIAAA's 1 drink assumes 12% ABV). UK: 175 mL at 13% = 2.3 units; servings 125/175/250 mL. Varietal records (Cabernet, Merlot, Pinot Noir) are similar.

drinks.name: Rosé Wine
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'wine, rose' (9.6 g alcohol/100 g -> ~12.1% ABV). Dry Provence-style rosés have less sugar than this average.

drinks.name: Sake (Japanese rice wine)

source.name: Japan Standard Tables of Food Composition (8th rev., 2023 suppl.), MEXT: food 16001, sake, regular (futsushu)
source.crossCheck: USDA SR 'Alcoholic beverage, rice (sake)' (167723) gives 16.1 g alcohol and 134 kcal per 100 g, implying ~20% ABV, which is atypical (flagged in Part B); not used.

drinks.notes: MEXT per 100 g: 82.4 g water, 107 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 4.9 g carbohydrate (2.5 g available carbohydrate as monosaccharides), 2 mg Na, 5 mg K, 12.3 g ethanol. Converted with USDA's sake density (29.1 g per fl oz = 0.984 g/mL): 12.1 g ethanol/100 mL = 15.3% ABV, matching typical 15-16% labels. A 180 mL go (the traditional serving) = 21.8 g ethanol = 1.6 US standard drinks. Sugar is not reported separately (null). Premium grades (junmai, ginjo) are similar.

drinks.name: Sparkling Wine (Champagne/Prosecco/Cava)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central, FDC 2710687 'Wine, sparkling', read directly from the FDC portal endpoint (Nov 2026)

corrections.reason: Direct USDA re-pull: water 87.93 g/100 g x 0.995 = 87.49 (entry 87.46). All other fields (75 kcal, 9.5 g alcohol, sugars 1.0, carbs 2.31, K 74, Na 5 per 100 g) confirmed.

drinks.notes: FNDDS 'Wine, sparkling' (9.5 g alcohol/100 g -> ~12.0% ABV; FNDDS '1 glass' = 180 g). Typical flute ~120-150 mL. Sweetness labels (Brut Nature < 3 g/L sugar up to Doux > 50 g/L) change sugar substantially.

drinks.name: White Wine
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'wine, table, white': 10.3 g alcohol/100 g x 0.993 = 10.2 g/100 mL = ~13.0% ABV. Sweet/late-harvest whites have more sugar (SR 173202). UK 175 mL glass at 12% = 2.1 units.

drinks.name: Chicken Broth
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'Soup, chicken broth, ready-to-serve'. Density taken as 1.00 (USDA's 1 cup = 249 g would imply ~1.05). Very high sodium (~890 mg per cup); reduced-sodium broth (FDC 172888) ~231 mg/100 g; bone broths have more protein (~4-10 g per cup by brand). Brothy soups can use this entry; chunky soups should not be logged as drinks.

drinks.name: Apple Cider Vinegar Drink (ready-to-drink)

source.name: Bragg Refreshers ACV Ginger Lemon Honey label (via retailer listing)

drinks.notes: Per 8 fl oz: 40 kcal, 9 g added sugar, 10 mg sodium. DIY: 2 tbsp Bragg ACV-honey blend in 8 oz water = 35 kcal, 10 g sugar per glass (~267 mL). Plain ACV (1 tbsp) in water adds ~3 kcal and negligible sugar. Shrubs/drinking vinegars (e.g., Pok Pok Som) are concentrates - log diluted volume. No national-database record exists.

drinks.name: Kombucha

source.name: Yang J, et al. Microbial and Chemical Profiles of Commercial Kombucha Products. Nutrients 2022;14(3):670 (PMC8838605)

corrections.reason: Caffeine was null. USDA re-pull shows FNDDS lists 11 mg/100 g (recipe-based); measured commercial products (HPLC, n=9) are much lower, so the literature median is used with a range that spans both. Macros confirmed unchanged.

drinks.notes: FNDDS 'Tea, kombucha' re-pulled directly from USDA (per 100 g: water 94.91, 16 kcal, carbs 3.98, sugars 3.99, protein 0.1, Na 2, K 4, caffeine 11 mg); converted with density 1.01; all macro values confirmed. Cross-check GT's Synergy labels: 50-60 kcal and 12-16 g sugar per 16 oz (~2.5-3.4 g sugar/100 mL). Caffeine: the FNDDS 11 mg/100 g is a recipe estimate from brewed tea and ignores fermentation losses and dilution; HPLC of nine US commercial kombuchas (Yang et al., Nutrients 2022) found 15-113 ug/mL, median 29 ug/mL (2.9 mg/100 mL); the 113 ug/mL product had added green-coffee-bean caffeine. Default 2.9 mg/100 mL, range 1.5-11.3 (the upper end also covers the FNDDS figure). Commercial 'non-alcoholic' kombucha must stay <0.5% ABV in the US, but the same study measured up to 1.29% ethanol in one product; raw/'hard' kombuchas are 3-7% ABV (log those as alcohol).

drinks.name: Horchata (Mexican rice drink)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.description: Beverages, Horchata, as served in restaurant
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Horchata, made with water' (2710602): 88 kcal, 8.1 g sugar, 78 g water per 100 g; 'made with milk' (2710603): 91 kcal, 9.6 g sugar.

drinks.notes: USDA SR restaurant horchata (water analysed in 3 samples): per 100 g 54 kcal, 9.4 g sugar, 87.1 g water. Converted with the FNDDS horchata portion weight (248 g per cup = 1.048 g/mL) because the SR record's only portion (228 g per cup) looks like it includes ice. The FNDDS recipe-based versions are thicker (78 g water, ~90 kcal/100 g); restaurant horchata is closer to the SR value. Spanish horchata de chufa (tiger nut) is a different drink. Listed as a Part B v2 gap.

drinks.name: Hot Chocolate (made with milk)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'Milk, chocolate beverage, hot cocoa, homemade'. Density 1.05 g/mL. ~5 mg caffeine per cup from cocoa. Coffee-shop hot chocolates with whipped cream are richer (Starbucks grande ~370-400 kcal).

drinks.name: Hot Cocoa (mix made with water)
drinks.notes: USDA SR 'Cocoa mix, powder, prepared with water'. Density 1.04 g/mL.
